Otemae geiko Fumino [Gion Kobu] hosting tea ceremony

The Japanese take tea really seriously. They have a tea ceremony! There are even different types of tea ceremony. One geiko and one maiko are needed for the kind of tea ceremony we talk about on this subverse: an otemae (geiko preparing the tea), and an ohikae (maiko distributing the tea).

In this photo, geiko Fumino from Fukushima yakata is otemae. She wears a special outfit and hairstyle only worn for tea ceremony. Her han-eri (collar) is folded over to see some of the red underneath. I believe that the reason the han-eri is worn this way is to set her apart from maiko, but it's possible that I'm wrong.

Geiko wear katsura (a wig) most of the time, but during odori tea ceremony, an otemae wears a special hairstyle called kyofuu shimada using her own hair. It's a gorgeous hairstyle.

After the odori, an otemae will attend a party with only nape oshiroi (white makeup), not on her face. This is to set her apart from the maiko who are there.

For some background, I'm a 17 year old white guy, I drive a stick shift, and I was driving over the speed limit to get home from the gym before midnight. He was nice enough to not give me a ticket, and I am extremely grateful for that, but damn was he a fucking asshole during the process.

I was going about 43 in a 35 at about 11:40 (past curfew), and he pulls me over, which is fine since I was speeding. Then he told me he pulled me over for "spinning my tires and speeding." After he does the whole process of getting my license information and coming back to tell me that I have a warning, I ask him "What does it mean to spin my tires," since I have no clue what that means and I want to know what not to do. I've never heard that term until tonight. He then asks, "Are you stupid? Do you really not know what spinning your tires means? I'm about to give you a ticket if you keep playing dumb with me." So I pretty much had to lie and say that I know what it means and that I won't do it again. He then much calls me stupid again for not knowing what it means and explains it and tells me not to play dumb again.

I wouldn't mind the officer telling me what I did wrong in a professional way, but he sounded like my sister when I asked him to explain something that I didn't know (using that really condescending tone while implying that he is smarter than me). I bit my tongue, but I really wanted to ask him what he did when he was my age after he asked if I was stupid. Was he reading books by Adam Smith (both 1960s and 1700s), Karl Marx, and Lord Keynes for fun like me? Was he getting all A's in all honors classes because he studied his ass off and did all the work and a little research on the side like me? Was he studying advanced music theory so that he could be a better guitar teacher to his students like me? I'd be willing to bet my college fund that he wasn't doing any of those, so before he calls me stupid because I asked what something meant, he should really contemplate calling someone stupid when he doesn't know their background, especially when you're in a position in society that doesn't require much education and already has a bad reputation for abusing power.

I don't hate cops, because I know that they do more than pull people over for speeding tickets and they have helped people that I know. I will say thank you to any cops reading this that do their job professionally.

At least I know that when I'm his age I'm going to be an actuary or an economist and earn my money in a guilt-free way and not bully 17 year olds at midnight to boost my ego.
